title: Part 1 Blog Post
summary: I made a theme toggle feature for my website. I encountered some challenges and learned a few things along the way.
content:
This feature switches between dark mode and light mode with the user clicking the button to switch between the two.
I approached by following the template initially and then adding in other pieces that were needed through research via the internet.
For example, I needed to make a button so the code provided in the template would work properly.
Challenges I encountered: finding a way to represent the current theme while also ensuring the button is still visible; ensuring that once the dark theme or light theme was added the other elements on the page were visible; preventing the flashing of the wrong theme during transition from one page to another.
What I learned: the CSS I used in the theme folder was lower precedence compared to the external folder CSS, so if I wanted a consistent theme that varies by current theme I needed the theme folder to determine that.
Another thing I learned was that the theme of the page should be set at the top so it renders right away, instead of waiting for script execution.

title: Part 2 Blog Post
summary: I made a feature that dynamically loads the header and footer. I encountered a few challenges and learned a few things along the way.
content:
This feature dynamically loads the header and footer of the page.
I approached this by creating a component.js file that contains the code to load the header and footer.
I then included this script in each HTML file where I wanted the header and footer to be loaded.
Challenges I encountered: ensuring that the header and footer were loaded correctly on each page; making sure that the styles for the header and footer were applied correctly; dealing with any potential conflicts between the header/footer styles and the page styles.
What I learned: how to use JavaScript to dynamically load content into a webpage; how to structure my code to make it reusable across multiple pages; how to troubleshoot issues related to dynamic content loading.

title: Part 3 Blog Post
summary: I made a feature that dynamically loads the blog posts. I encountered a few challenges and learned a few things along the way.
content:
This feature dynamically loads the blog posts from a JSON file.
I approached this by following the template provided and added my theme toggle code.
Challenges I encountered: ensuring that the blog posts were being shown on the page; ensuring that the read more link was visible in both light and dark modes; dealing with any potential conflicts between the blog post styles and the page styles.
What I learned: I learnt that using hyphens for date will result in JavaScript using UTC midnight by default, and I also learnt how to sort objects in descending order by date.

title: Part 4 Blog Post
summary: I made a feature that validates the inputs sent by the user in the contact form. I encountered a few challenges and learned a few things along the way.
content:
This feature validates the form as the client fills out, providing clear actionable feedback as they try to fill out the form.
I approached it by following the template and searching up any gaps in my understanding on the internet to get a better understanding, like for example an inline error message and what that looked like exactly so I could see if I had done it correctly.
Challenges encountered: - Input text is not visible during dark mode - Showing an inline error for the message box - Showing a success message after form was validated.
What I learnt: Having a generic CSS text color for the form will cause problems down the line so it is important to ensure it is set in a future-proof manner.
What an inline error message box looks like and how to make one.
